20 A platform is suspended by four steel wires. Each wire is 5.0 m long and has a diameter of
3.0 mm. The Young modulus of steel is 2.1  1011
Pa.
steel wires
steel wires
200 kg
platform
The wires obey Hooke’s law when a load of mass 200 kg is placed on the platform.
How far will the platform descend because of the extension of the wires?
A
1.7  10–4
m
B
4.1  10–4
m
C
1.7  10–3
m
D
6.6  10–3
m

hints: Notice the 200 kg weight is shared equally by four wires, so find the tensile force $F$ in one 5.0 m wire.
Recall Young modulus as $E = (F/A)/(e/L)$ and that the wire area needs the radius $1.5 \text{ mm}$ from the 3.0 mm diameter.
Rearrange to $e = FL/(AE)$ for one wire and check that the platform descent equals the extension $e$ of each wire.
walkthrough: Total weight on the platform is $W = mg = 200 \times 9.81 \approx 1960 \text{ N}$. Shared by four identical wires, the force in one wire is $F = W/4 \approx 490 \text{ N}$.
Cross-sectional area of one wire uses radius $r = 3.0/2 \text{ mm} = 1.5 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$: $A = \pi r^2 = \pi(1.5 \times 10^{-3})^2 \approx 7.07 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^2$.
Young modulus relates stress and strain: $E = \text{stress}/\text{strain} = (F/A)/(e/L)$. Rearranged for extension, $e = FL/(AE)$.
Numerator is about $2450 \text{ N m}$ and denominator is about $1.48 \times 10^6 \text{ N}$, giving $e \approx 1.65 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$.
All wires extend equally, so the platform descends by this extension, about $1.7 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: This is about ten times too small and does not follow from $e = FL/(AE)$ with the 5.0 m length and correct wire area.

B.explanation: This is four times too small because it uses the 3.0 mm diameter as the radius, making the area four times too large.

C.explanation: Using one quarter of the 200 kg weight per wire in $e = FL/(AE)$ gives about $1.7 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$.

D.explanation: This is four times too large because it puts the full $200g$ weight on one wire instead of sharing it equally between the four wires.
